pr_title: release-22.1: fix unstable sort in SSTSink
pr_body:
This patch includes a backport of
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/83102.

The focus of this patch is fixing the unstable sort described in #95445. Previously, we would sort only on the basis of the start key of two backup files returned as part of an ExportResponse. This could result in older revisions of a key getting sorted and flushed to the underlying SSTWriter before new revisions, resulting in out-of-order writes, causing the backup to fail. We saw this in the support issue https://github.com/cockroachlabs/support/issues/1998 and have a test TestExportRevisionsWithTimestampPagination that failed under stress.

To fix this unstable sort we now use the following algorithm:

1. Sort on start key of the backup files.
2. If start key is the same, sort on end key of the backup files.
3. If end key is the same, sort in descending order on the end key timestamp of the files as both files are guaranteed to only contain revisions of the same key.

Fixes: #95445

Release note (bug fix): Fixes a bug where a backup of keys with many revisions would fail with "pebble: keys must be added in order".

Release justification: high impact bug fix to prevent failing backups

issue_context.title: backupccl: unstable sort in the SSTSink of the backup processor results in out of order writes
issue_context.body:
In 22.1 bulkio.backup.split_keys_on_timestamps defaults to true. This means that a key with several revisions can be paginated across ExportRequests with some revisions being returned in the first response, and the remaining in subsequent responses. These responses are then buffered in a queue and sorted based on their start key - https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blame/aa4881fe34e1b9cb607799e238bace73bd8a0820/pkg/ccl/backupccl/backup_processor.go#L712. The problem is the sort here isn’t stable since it does not take into account the timestamp if the key is the same. If we have two SSTs with the same start key but different timestamps we could get into a situation where we have two ExportResponses [a@6, a@5, a@4] and [a@3, a@2, a@1] that get sorted {[a@3, a@2, a@1] , [a@6, a@5, a@4]} in our queue.

When we go to write the second response SST to the sstwriter https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/aa4881fe34e1b9cb607799e238bace73bd8a0820/pkg/ccl/backupccl/backup_processor.go#L815 evaluates to false not forcing a flush of the underlying file and we end up writing a@6 in an SST where the highest ts we’ve written is a@3 resulting in an out of order error.

Jira issue: CRDB-23518
comments: Fixed in all the affected versions, closing!

review_comments: If you wanted, I suppose we could randomize the order of these
